level1.text: A ball is released from rest, and air resistance is ignored. What is the speed of the ball when $3.0\,\text{s}$ have passed since the start of the fall?
An apple comes off a branch and falls from rest to the ground in $0.80\,\text{s}$. Air resistance is ignored. What is the speed of the apple when it hits the ground?

On the surface of the Moon the acceleration of free fall is $1.62\,\text{m/s}^2$. An astronaut drops a stone, which falls from rest for $4.0\,\text{s}$. What is the speed of the stone after this time?
The $(t, v)$ graph of a freely falling object is a straight line through the points $(0\,\text{s};\, 0\,\text{m/s})$ and $(5.0\,\text{s};\, 49\,\text{m/s})$. What is the acceleration of free fall?
On Mars the acceleration of free fall is $3.71\,\text{m/s}^2$. An object falls on Mars from rest for $6.0\,\text{s}$ without air resistance. What is the speed of the object?

level2.text: A ball is released from rest and hits the ground at a speed of $12.0\,\text{m/s}$. Air resistance is ignored. How long did the ball fall?
A stone is released from rest and hits the water at a speed of $54.0\,\text{km/h}$. Air resistance is ignored. How long did the stone fall?
The speed of a falling object is $12.0\,\text{m/s}$ at some moment, and there is no air resistance. How large is the speed $1.50\,\text{s}$ later?

The speed of a freely falling object is measured at two moments: $9.7\,\text{m/s}$ at the moment $t = 1.0\,\text{s}$ and $29.3\,\text{m/s}$ at the moment $t = 3.0\,\text{s}$. Calculate the acceleration of free fall from these measurements.

level3.text: In a vacuum chamber two balls with masses $0.50\,\text{kg}$ and $4.0\,\text{kg}$ are dropped from rest at the same time. How many times as large is the speed of the heavier ball as the speed of the lighter ball when $1.5\,\text{s}$ have passed since the start of the fall?

An unknown planet has no atmosphere. There the speed of a stone dropped from rest is $14.8\,\text{m/s}$ after $4.0\,\text{s}$. After how many seconds from the start of the fall is the speed of the stone $30.0\,\text{m/s}$?

A ball is dropped from rest in air, and its speed is measured to be $25.0\,\text{m/s}$ after $3.00\,\text{s}$. By how many $\text{m/s}$ is the speed smaller than the speed the ball would have in free fall without air resistance?
